title: Knowledge grounding: which data can a Copilot Studio agent answer from?
summary: Hold: the checklist gives Documents setting options that do not exist; Microsoft documents Yes and No, not None, All and Custom. The tenant graph guidance also omits the same-tenant Copilot licence and configured semantic index prerequisites, which matter before enabling it for unlicensed users.

claims.claim: Knowledge sources are managed at Security > Data and privacy > Knowledge sources for agents > environment group or environment > Manage knowledge sources.
claims.quote: In the side pane, choose whether to sort by Environment groups or by Environments. Select the environment group or environment that you want to configure.
claims.fix: Include the omitted selector in both representations of controls[0].ui.path: Security > Data and privacy > Knowledge sources for agents > Environment groups or Environments > environment group or environment > Manage knowledge sources.

claims.claim: A data policy connector is blocked at Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Next > Next > connector > three dots > Block.
claims.quote: Select the three dots (⋮) next to the connector, and then: To prevent agent makers from using the features associated with the connector, select Block.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Classification <group> -Connectors $connectors moves connectors into a specified data policy group.
claims.quote: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy [-PolicyName] <String> [-Classification] <String> [-Connectors] <Object[]> [[-ApiVersion] <String>] [<CommonParameters>]

claims.claim: Dataverse search is configured at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse search in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Manage. In the Manage pane, select Environments. On the Environments page, select an environment. In the command bar, select Settings. Expand Product, then select Features.

claims.claim: The maker's Tenant graph grounding with semantic search control is on the agent's Generative AI settings page.

claims.quote: Custom: Select which public websites agents can use. Agents reference them in priority order, starting with the first URL. Select either Allow or Deny under Access for each URL.

claims.claim: Dataverse knowledge sources require Dataverse search in the environment.
claims.quote: To use this knowledge source, Copilot Studio agents must use Dataverse search. If you can't add a Dataverse table to an agent, ask your administrator to turn on Dataverse search in your environment.

claims.claim: A Dataverse knowledge source supports up to 15 tables.
claims.quote: You can add up to 15 Dataverse tables per knowledge source.

claims.claim: Dataverse table knowledge requires Authenticate with Microsoft.
claims.quote: Dataverse tables as knowledge sources require you to set your agent's authentication to Authenticate with Microsoft. The other two options, No authentication and Authenticate manually aren't currently supported.

claims.claim: Generative orchestration filters more than 25 different knowledge sources with an internal GPT model.
claims.quote: Generative orchestration filters knowledge sources by using an internal GPT model when there are more than 25 different knowledge sources. Files uploaded to the agent aren't part of the 25 knowledge source search limit.
claims.fix: Append to the filtering sentence: 'Uploaded files are excluded from this count.'

claims.where: What it is: A different sense
claims.claim: Work IQ lets agents reach Microsoft 365 and business data for grounding.
claims.quote: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer that enables agents to access and reason over organizational and business data, context, and tools.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/ to sources for the Work IQ distinction; the linked wiki concept is not Microsoft evidence.

claims.claim: Makers choose which knowledge sources their agents reference, subject to administrator restrictions.
claims.quote: Makers can choose which types of knowledge sources their agents can reference. The Knowledge sources for agents setting in Power Platform admin center controls access to sources such as SharePoint, OneDrive, public websites, and documents such as files.

claims.where: Why it matters: opening; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft's preview documentation does not state the default of Knowledge sources for agents.
claims.quote: Searched: "Knowledge sources for agents" "default" "published". Read https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/knowledge-sources-for-agents-rule in full; options are listed but no default is stated.

claims.claim: The preview setting page does not say whether it applies to already-published agents.
claims.quote: Searched: "Knowledge sources for agents" "default" "published". Read https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/knowledge-sources-for-agents-rule in full; it does not discuss existing published agents.

claims.where: Why it matters: Allow ungrounded responses
claims.claim: No admin-centre setting for Allow ungrounded responses is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow ungrounded responses" "admin center"; site:learn.microsoft.com "Allow ungrounded responses" admin policy. Opened https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/knowledge-copilot-studio; no admin-centre control found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Ungrounded answers
claims.claim: Allow ungrounded responses permits answers from general knowledge without a source or tool.
claims.quote: When you turn on the Allow ungrounded responses setting, your agent can respond by using the model's general knowledge, even when it doesn't use any knowledge sources or tools.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: With Allow ungrounded responses off, responses from turns without a source or tool are blocked, including history-only follow-ups.
claims.quote: When you turn off this setting, the agent blocks any response generated in a turn where it didn't use a knowledge source or tool. This condition means the response is blocked if the agent answers a question from conversation history or general knowledge

claims.claim: Turning off Allow ungrounded responses does not prevent combining general knowledge with retrieved content.
claims.quote: The agent's underlying model might still incorporate general knowledge when it combines this knowledge with information it retrieves from knowledge sources or tools.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: With Allow ungrounded responses off, source-grounded answers require an in-text citation.
claims.quote: When you turn off Allow ungrounded responses, the agent returns an answer from a knowledge source only when the answer includes an in-text citation to that source.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: A correct answer without the required citation is withheld.
claims.quote: Occasionally, the model generates a correct answer from a knowledge source but doesn't include a citation for it. When that happens, the agent withholds the answer and responds as though it didn't find any information.

claims.claim: Copilot Credits are the usage meter for the described grounded answers.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the unit that measures agent usage.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: generative answer charging
claims.claim: The billing page says generative answers incur charges unless created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 without tenant graph grounding.
claims.quote: Agents incur charges for generative answer responses unless the agent is created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 and the response doesn't leverage tenant graph grounding.

claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding is optional and can be turned on or off per agent.

claims.claim: Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot licences use tenant graph grounding semantic search by default.
claims.quote: By default, all users with the Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses use tenant graph grounding semantic search.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: tenant graph; controls[4].note
claims.claim: The page tells readers they can enable tenant graph grounding for unlicensed users at extra cost without stating the tenant licence and semantic index prerequisites.
claims.quote: This feature requires the agent to share a tenant with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. It also requires that a semantic index is configured for use. To use a semantic index, the Microsoft 365 Copilot license must be assigned to at least one user in the enterprise.
claims.fix: After the extra-cost sentence and in the control note, add: 'This requires a configured semantic index and at least one user assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence in the agent's tenant.' Keep the existing generative orchestration and Authenticate with Microsoft requirements.

claims.claim: Files added through Upload files > SharePoint are stored in Dataverse.
claims.quote: When you use Upload files > SharePoint as a knowledge source, your files are stored in Dataverse, where they're processed and indexed for use.

claims.claim: These SharePoint files consume Dataverse data storage.
claims.quote: Your files and folders remain in Dataverse, so they do consume data storage.

claims.claim: Disallowing Documents uploads blocks only local file uploads.
claims.quote: Configuring Documents knowledge source to not allow uploads only prevents local file uploads. It doesn't prevent makers from adding files from SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive uploads must instead be restricted with SharePoint + OneDrive.
claims.quote: To not allow uploads from SharePoint or OneDrive, configure SharePoint + OneDrive to not allow access.

claims.claim: The upload files method lets anyone with permission to the agent access the file.
claims.quote: The upload files method allows anyone with permission to the agent to access the file.

claims.claim: SharePoint sources verify the user's credentials before answering from a file.
claims.quote: With SharePoint, the user's credentials are verified to ensure they have permission to access the file before providing responses.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Dataverse search; What to check
claims.claim: Turning off Dataverse search removes its index within 12 hours.
claims.quote: Turning off Dataverse search deprovisions and removes the index within 12 hours.

claims.claim: Rebuilding the Dataverse search index can take an hour or more, or a couple of days for large organizations.
claims.quote: If you turn on Dataverse search after it's been off for 12 hours, it creates a fresh index that needs to go through a full sync. Syncing can take an hour or more for average size organizations, and a couple of days for large organizations.

claims.where: What to check: authentication bullet; Governance controls table

claims.quote: Compare each agent's user authentication with the sources it uses; SharePoint, Dataverse and connector sources need it. The table covers knowledge source types, the SharePoint upload connector, Dataverse search, ungrounded responses and tenant graph grounding.
claims.fix: Remove the authentication checklist bullet; retain the already-supported authentication prerequisites in What it is. This corrects the checklist/table mismatch without adding a control row.
